kernelSdk.note: A DEVELOPMENT vendor, made on 2026-10-08 with the hub's scripts/vendor-sdk.mjs from hub main c8514c5c (#483). Hub main gained seven merged PRs for this client since the vendor before (1e5f6ed9, 27ef8a3d…): #482 synthetic comment examples, #477 Spenders stats, #480 awaiting-reply, #478 archive feed, #479 claim and send custody, #481 audience-new, #483 held sends (dashboard). Against 27ef8a3d… the contract only adds: the six client routes (clientConversationFeed, clientSpenderStats, clientSpenderAwaitingReply, clientFanClaim, clientFanClaimStatus, clientAudienceNew), the two cabinet routes clientSendCustodyResolve and clientSendCustodyList (never called), and the narrow token's scopes for the six; no existing operation or schema changed, so the SDK reads every answer of a hub on 27ef8a3d… as before. The prod hub still runs 27ef8a3d… until the owner deploys: its bootstrap declares none of archive-feed-v1, spenders-stats-v1, awaiting-reply-v1, preview-send-custody-v1, audience-new-v1, so those features read hub_not_ready and the hub layer never calls their routes. The release rule stays: a release is vendored only from a deployed hub commit (the release gate refuses an SDK hash the prod health does not list in compatibleClientSdks). Re-vendor with the same script, then update this pin in the same commit.
